name: prsmflush
image: prsmflush.bin (B/I/D/C cases, differential) + prsmflush_smm.bin (case A, witness)
description: Executable-invalidation CONTRACT regression (was: consumption-only). The consumption fix (rtl/core/core.sv) gates every fast-serve decision (sfetch_fast / pipe_bytes_ok / v_bytes_ok / uop_hit) with exec_issue_ok = !exec_flush_all, diverts S_PIPE to a post-edge refill, and wires the canonical I-cache's flush_all to exec_flush_all (it was tied off, so a flush could refill one way while the stale line stayed valid in the other -- duplicate valid tags in a set, hit priority deciding what executes). This test now proves the whole contract per flush source: the stale line is placed in way 0 in one subcase and way 1 in the other (every case fills a same-set conflict line -- a lone `ret` at target+0x1000 -- BEFORE the stale line, so the stale line is the most-recently-filled at the flush edge and the refill must land on the conflict's way), the +ven_icflushlog probe (sim-only, rtl/mem/icache.sv) must show the stale line's {set,way,tag,ptag} at the flush edge, the set's valid bits all zero one clock later, and only then the refill; and the executed bytes after the flush must be the NEW ones. Flush sources covered: CR3 reload (B1/B2), INVLPG (I1/I2 -- implemented as a conservative full TLB flush joining the same pulse), INVD/WBINVD (D1/D2, cache_inv_go), A20 edge (C1/C2), and RSM (case A, rsm_ctx_restore -> tlb_flush -> tlb_flush_q). External flush (the ao486 PS->PL daemon pulse) is not reachable from a bare-metal image on this TB; the ven_l1d side of it is covered by the l1 gates.
way_placement_mechanics: The I-cache lookup is linear-tagged and its hit LRU touches do not move the replacement victim (the touch ports only confirm hits), so fills strictly alternate the two ways. Each subcase owns a FRESH target line (its own PT1 slot + frames) so no subcase inherits a resident line; the fill parity then alternates the stale line's absolute way between consecutive subcases. The probe log is the placement evidence -- the gate requires ways {0,1} across each flush-source pair. A broken flush is caught three ways at once: the verification call hits the stale line and writes the OLD marker (behavioral), the ICACHE/DUP-TAG sim assertion fires if a refill ever shares a set with a stale valid tag (structural), and the probe log ordering pre -> post(empty) -> refill is graded per case (contract).

case_map.B1/B2 (CR3 reload, prsmflush.bin): paging on. B1: call the 0x401000 conflict ret, call 0x400000 (OLD stub in frame 0x800000 writes B_OLD to 0x2204, fills), remap PT1[0] -> 0x801000, reload CR3, call 0x400000 -- must execute NEW (B_NEW). B2: the same shape on a fresh line (0x402000, conflict 0x403000, frames 0x806000/0x807000, markers 0x2210/0x2214). Fail codes 0x11/0x12 (B1), 0x15/0x16 (B2)
case_map.I1/I2 (INVLPG, prsmflush.bin): same shape at 0x404000/0x406000 (conflicts 0x405000/0x407000, frames 0x808000/0x809000 and 0x80A000/0x80B000, markers 0x2218/0x221C and 0x2220/0x2224), flush source `invlpg (eax)` -- the decoder accepts the plain register-indirect form; no memory access is issued, matching the golden. Fail codes 0x17/0x18, 0x19/0x1A
case_map.D1/D2 (INVD/WBINVD, prsmflush.bin): CONTRACT-ONLY at 0x408000/0x40A000: the backing bytes do not change -- a CPU store would snoop-invalidate the line by its physical tag and test the snoop instead of INVD. The probe log proves the line was valid at the cache_inv_go edge and empty one clock later; the re-executed stub (D_NEW -> 0x2228, D2_NEW -> 0x222C) proves the refetch. D1 uses INVD (0F 08), D2 WBINVD (0F 09). Fail codes 0x1B/0x1C
case_map.C1/C2 (A20 edge, prsmflush.bin): A20 on (write-only port-0x92 toggle -- see oracle_notes), conflict ret at identity-mapped 0x100000 (C1) / 0x102000 (C2), call 0x101000 / 0x103000 (OLD bytes fill); A20 off (a20_flush); call again -- must alias to phys 0x1000 / 0x3000 (NEW bytes); A20 back on (a second flush, which the probe also logs: it sees the alias refill line). Markers 0x2208/0x220C (C1), 0x2230/0x2234 (C2). Fail codes 0x13/0x14 (C1), 0x1D/0x1E (C2)
case_map.A (SMM/RSM, prsmflush_smm.bin, two round: the stale line is an SMM fill of a REMAPPED linear address: the mainline runs with paging ON and linear 0x40000 -> phys 0x80000 (the NEW stub); SMM fetches are unpaged, so the handler's 32-bit call to the stub fills phys 0x40000 (the OLD stub) under linear tag 0x40 with physical identity 0x40; the handler redirects the save-map resume EIP to 0x40000 and RSMs; the resumed fetch must refill from phys 0x80000 (probe: refill ptag 00080), never serve the SMM line (without the flush the linear lookup hits it and OLD32 executes). This replaces the earlier rewrite-the-backing design, which was VACUOUS for the I-cache arrays: the core's own store snoop invalidates a store-rewritten line by its physical tag before RSM ever runs. Round 1 calls the stub only, round 2 calls two dummies first -- the extra fill flips the way parity, so the stale line sits in the opposite way (measured: round 1 way 1, round 2 way 0). Fail codes 0x21/0x22 (round 1), 0x24/0x25 (round 2), 0x23 (RSM GPR restore)

witnesses.prsmflush.bin final record: edi = 0xB0020002 (B_NEW), esi = 0xC0020002 (C_NEW), ebx = 0xB0010001 (B_OLD fill proof), ebp = 0xC0010001 (C_OLD fill proof), ecx = 0xB0080008 (I2_NEW), edx = 0x600D00F4 (pass magic | 0xF4 port). Fully differential vs the QEMU golden (4650 records, EQUIVALENT)
witnesses.prsmflush.bin probe log (+ven_icflushlog: per case tag (B 00400/00402, I 00404/00406, D 00408/0040a, C 00101/00103): a `pre` line with the stale tag resident at the case's flush edge, a `post set=0 valid=00` one clock later, and the refill `fill` of that tag only after the post; each pair's stale ways must be {0,1} (measured 1/0 for all four pairs)
witnesses.prsmflush_smm.bin final record: edi = 0x5A4D0002 (NEW32 -- the post-RSM fetch refilled the NEW frame; THE discriminator), esi = 0x5A4D0001 (OLD32 -- the in-SMM fill executed), ebp = 0x5A4D900D (RSM restored the interrupted GPR state), ebx = 0x52455421 'RET!' (mainline resumed), ecx = 0x42, edx = 0x600D00F4. Witness-graded (no differential golden -- see oracle_notes)
witnesses.prsmflush_smm.bin probe log: two RSM flush events with pre tag=00040 ptag=00040 (the unpaged SMM fill) resident -- round 1 in way 1, round 2 in way 0 -- each followed by post valid=00 and a refill fill with ptag 00080 (the remapped frame, proving the resumed context re-walked the page)

oracle_notes: CASE A (SMM) HAS NO DIFFERENTIAL GOLDEN -- the psmm oracle infeasibility, restated: the qemu-system-i386 gdbstub single-step path (gen_trace.py --system) single-steps with SSTEP_NOIRQ, which masks CPU_INTERRUPT_SMI, and the stub has no SMM awareness (no HF_SMM in the g-packet), so a golden trace can never contain the SMM context. The scenario IS expressible free-running (the APIC self-IPI fires SMI under qemu, and the save-map EIP slot sits at SMBASE+0xFFF0 in both the P5 layout the RTL implements and QEMU's P6 layout), so prsmflush_smm.bin runs to the isa-debug-exit under free-running QEMU (status 133, verified) -- only the trace is infeasible. Grading: RTL final-record witnesses + the +ven_icflushlog probe contract + the QEMU free-run exit status, the pselnull/psmm pattern.

CASE C (A20) RUNS THE RTL SIDE WITH `--system --cosim`: port-0x92 I/O (any IN/OUT other than the out-0xf4 terminator) is a deliberate LOUD HALT in the plain --system testbench; --cosim is the sanctioned enable (the same flag run-a20-gate.sh uses): it only enables the io_* seam and selects the -cpu pentium reset EDX, leaving the retire/trace semantics identical, so the QEMU golden remains a valid differential oracle (measured: 4650 records EQUIVALENT).

CASE C uses WRITE-ONLY port-0x92 toggles: an IN from port 0x92 returns 0x00 in QEMU but 0xFF on the TB's io bus (empty-slot convention) -- an environment difference, not architecture. Writing known values (0x02 enable / 0x00 disable) keeps the case fully differential.

CR0.CD: CR0 resets to 0x6000_0010, so CD (and NW) are SET out of reset -- architecturally correct for a P5, and a real BIOS clears them after POST. With CD set the core marks every instruction fill non-cacheable (fill_nocache), no line is ever retained, and the way-occupancy contract is unobservable (every fetch refills). Both images therefore clear CD+NW as the first protected-mode instruction. The differential is unaffected (QEMU does not model caches; the CR0 write is architecturally identical on both sides).

INVLPG decodes to a conservative FULL TLB flush in this core (IA-32 allows invalidating more than the named page), driven by the same tlb_flush pulse as MOV CR3 -- so the I1/I2 flush reaches exec_flush_all one registered cycle after the S_EXEC retire, exactly like B1/B2. QEMU invalidates only the named page; the difference is invisible in the trace (over-invalidation can only cost extra walks).

the D1/D2 INVD/WBINVD cases are contract-only BY NECESSITY in this build: the core's own store snoop (icsnp_v1/v2) invalidates any store-rewritten line by its physical tag, so no store-based backing change can leave a stale I-cache line for INVD to kill; and without an L1/DMA agent in the canonical TB nothing else can change the backing. The probe-log contract (valid at the cache_inv_go edge, empty one clock later, refill after) is the honest gradeable content.

pre-fix behaviour (from reading the old logic, not a rebuild): the flush events cleared the executable arrays at a clock edge, but sfetch_fast / pipe_bytes_ok / v_bytes_ok / uop_hit were NOT gated on exec_flush_all, so a fast path could issue/retire from a line the flush is killing -- the deterministic case is RSM, where smm_flush is high the cycle after exit and a cached SMRAM line could retire one stale instruction (the fix comment in rtl/core/core.sv). For case A that means: the resumed fetch at linear 0x40000 serves the stale SMM-filled line and OLD32 executes (0x2100 stays 0 -- fail 0x21/0x24). For the B/I/C remap cases: one more OLD execution after the flush (the NEW marker slot stays 0).

commands: qemu-system-i386 -display none -machine pc -m 32 -device isa-debug-exit,iobase=0xf4,iosize=0x04 -bios verif/sys/tests/prsmflush/prsmflush.bin  -> exit 133
qemu-system-i386 ... -bios verif/sys/tests/prsmflush/prsmflush_smm.bin  -> exit 133 (free-run; SMM fires via the APIC self-IPI)
